name: semtimedop
synopsis: int semop(int semid, struct sembuf *sops, size_t nsops);
int semtimedop(int semid, struct sembuf *sops, size_t nsops, const struct timespec *_Nullable timeout);
description: semtimedop performs atomic operations on a System V semaphore set, similar to semop, but with an optional timeout to prevent indefinite blocking. It executes the specified operations on the semaphores or fails if the timeout expires.

parameters.name: sops
parameters.description: Pointer to an array of sembuf structures, each specifying an operation on a semaphore

parameters.name: nsops
parameters.description: Number of operations in the sops array

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Pointer to a timespec structure specifying the timeout, or NULL for no timeout

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and sets errno to indicate the error

errors.description: The argument nsops is greater than SEMOPM, the maximum number of operations allowed per system call
The calling process does not have the required permissions and does not have the CAP_IPC_OWNER capability
An operation could not proceed immediately and either IPC_NOWAIT was specified or the timeout expired
An address specified in sops or timeout is not accessible
For some operation, the value of sem_num is less than 0 or greater than or equal to the number of semaphores in the set
While blocked, the thread caught a signal
The semaphore set doesn’t exist, or semid is less than zero, or nsops has a non-positive value
The sem_flg of some operation specified SEM_UNDO and the system does not have enough memory
For some operation, sem_op + semval is greater than SEMVMX

bugs: When a process terminates with SEM_UNDO operations, semaphore values are decreased as far as possible (to zero) but not below, which may not fully undo the operations, potentially leading to inconsistencies.
examples: sops[0].sem_op = 0; /* Wait for value to equal 0 */
